details: About 4.7 million people are experiencing emergency, or IPC Phase 4, levels of food insecurity across Afghanistan. Food insecurity is compounded by a weak, contracting economy, declining remittances following the return of over 2.5 million people from Iran and Pakistan in 2025, and recent earthquakes that have further strained food stocks and livelihoods.

Israeli airstrikes and ground operations continue in Lebanon, despite the temporary ceasefire. At least 1.05 million people have been displaced since the start of the conflict in early March, with over 2,500 people killed and over 7,800 people injured.

US and Israeli airstrikes on Iran have displaced millions of people throughout March and April. Despite the ceasefire, millions remain displaced and humanitarian needs are high. At least 32,000 people have been injured, while over 2,300 people were killed. Please note, related impacts in other countries will be classified separately.

The Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) confirmed a new Ebola outbreak in Ituri province in the northeast of the DRC on 15 May. The outbreak is focused in and around Ituri's capital Bunia as well as the more remote, mining area of Mongbwalu. As of 27 July, there are at least 3,200 cases and 1,405 deaths, making this the fastest spreading Ebola outbreak documented. About 90% of all cases are in Ituri province, but cases are reported in North and South Kivu as well, and have recently spread to Haut-Uele and Tshopo provinces.

details: Nearly 200,000 people are experience catastrophic, or IPC5, levels of food insecurity across the Darfur and Kordofan states in Sudan, while 2.3 million others are experiencing emergency, or IPC4, levels. Darfur and the Kordofan states are seeing the most intense fighting in the country with many cities partially or fully blockaded, preventing food or supplies from reaching the population. There is credible risk of famine in parts of South Kordofan and North Darfur in particular, as the lean season approaches.  Please note, the current IPC assessment did not include figures for the rest of the country.

Non-state armed group activity has constrained food systems in Haiti, where more than 1.8 million people (1 million people within Port au Prince, and the Artibonite, Ouest, and Centre departments) face Emergency (IPC 4) levels of food insecurity. Further deterioration is expected in the coming months

Amid extreme violence in El Fasher by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), over 100,000 civilians have been displaced to nearby, with estimates of 60,000 people killed. The city has been besieged for nearly two years causing catastrophic levels of food insecurity among the affected population. Many civilians remain trapped in El Fasher with no access to aid or missing, and those who have managed to escape to safety have reported mass killings and sexual violence. Please note, this classification has increased due to updates to the classification system as well as new data that has been released.

details: Fighting between the Rwandan-backed armed group M23 and the Congolese armed forces (FARDC) has escalated in South Kivu, displacing over 1 million people since October. Fighting has been heaviest in Uvira, Walungu, Fizi, and Mwenga territories, within South Kivu, in the eastern DRC

Renewed fighting between the South Sudanese military (SSPDF) and their main opposition group, the Sudan's Peoples Liberation Army in Opposition (SPLA-iO), has displaced over 290,000 people in South Sudan's Jonglei, Upper Nile, and Unity states. Further clashes are expected as the SSPDF has ordered civilians and NGOs to evacuate opposition held territory as they prepare to retake the area.

details: Insecurity, displacement, and climate shocks are driving severe food insecurity in Borno state in Northeast Nigeria, with over 630,000 people experiencing emergency (IPC4) levels of food insecurity and over 15,000 experiencing catastrophic (IPC5) levels of food insecurity. Many of those people, including over half of those experiencing IPC5, are internally displaced. This comes as Borno state is also experiencing a cholera outbreak (NG521) and a resurgence in violence.

two powerful earthquakes measuring 7.5 and 7.2 on the Richter scale struck near Morón, around 160km west of the Venezuelan capital Caracas on the evening of 24th June. The damage is reported heaviest in La Guaira state, though Caracas is also significantly affected. As of 02 July, at least 3,800 people have been reported killed with over 16,000 injured, although figures are expected to rise as search and rescue operations continue.

Since  the Uganda Ministry of Health declared an Ebola virus outbreak on 15 May, at least 20 cases have been confirmed with 3 deaths. All cases in Uganda are linked to the original cross-border transmission from neighboring DRC. Uganda has activated surveillance and screening measures, and those who had come in contact with the cases are being quarantined.

details: South Sudan is facing high levels of food insecurity, with 27,856 people experiencing catastrophic or IPC5 levels of food insecurity, and more than 1.2 million people in emergency or IPC4 levels. Nearly half of the population is facing IPC 3 or higher food insecurity. This is driven largely by localized conflict, civil insecurity, and widespread flooding that has impacted agricultural lands and food production.
